definitions.explanation: A day associated with a particular Buddhist or Shinto deity, on which visiting the temple or shrine is believed to bring special blessings. By extension, the festive market or fair held on such days with food stalls and games.

examples.japanese: {縁日|えんにち}の{屋台|やたい}でたこ{焼|や}きを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought takoyaki at a stall at the fair.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもの{頃|ころ}、{近所|きんじょ}のお{寺|てら}の{縁日|えんにち}で{金魚|きんぎょ}すくいをするのが{楽|たの}しみだった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I looked forward to scooping goldfish at the fair at the neighborhood temple.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Originally, {縁日|えんにち} referred to days with a special karmic connection ({縁|えん}) to a particular deity, when visiting would bring extra merit. In modern usage, it primarily refers to the festive markets that spring up at temples and shrines, with food stalls ({屋台|やたい}), games like {金魚|きんぎょ}すくい (goldfish scooping) and {射的|しゃてき} (target shooting), and a lively atmosphere.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {縁日|えんにち}の{屋台|やたい}: festival stalls
- {縁日|えんにち}に{出|で}かける: to go out to a fair
- {縁日|えんにち}で{遊|あそ}ぶ: to enjoy oneself at a fair
